examples.text: Разумеется, мы не очень-то похожи на будущих пилотов, особенно когда поздней ночью возвращаемся домой с аэродрома и весь трамвай начинает принюхиваться и смотреть на нас с негодованием.

glosses: A sensation, pleasant or unpleasant, detected by inhaling air (or, the case of water-breathing animals, water) carrying airborne molecules of a substance.

examples.text: I love the smell of fresh bread.

The penetrating smell of cabbage reached the nose of Toad as he lay prostrate in his misery on the floor, and gave him the idea for a moment that perhaps life was not such a blank and desperate thing as he had imagined. But still he wailed, and kicked with his legs, and refused to be comforted. So the wise girl retired for the time, but, of course, a good deal of the smell of hot cabbage remained behind, as it will do, and Toad, between his sobs, sniffed and reflected, and gradually began to think new and inspiring thoughts: of chivalry, and poetry[…]

glosses: The sense that detects odours.
A conclusion or intuition that a situation is wrong, more complex than it seems, or otherwise inappropriate.

examples.text: I’m just saying, this has a bad smell to it.

glosses: To sense a smell or smells.

examples.text: I can smell fresh bread.
Smell the milk and tell me whether it's gone off.

glosses: To sense a smell or smells.
To detect or perceive; often with out.

examples.text: I smell a device.

glosses: Followed by like or of if descriptive: to have a particular smell, whether good or bad.

examples.text: The roses smell lovely.
Her feet smell of cheese.
The drunkard smelt like a brewery.
Philander went into the next room[…]and came back with a salt mackerel[…]. Next he put the mackerel in a fry-pan, and the shanty began to smell like a Banks boat just in from a v'yage.
Este's been losing sleep / Her husband's acting different and it smells like infidelity

glosses: Followed by like or of if descriptive: to have a particular smell, whether good or bad.
To smell of; to have a smell of

examples.text: I do smell all horse-piss

glosses: Followed by like or of if descriptive: to have a particular smell, whether good or bad.
To smell bad; to stink.

examples.text: Ew, this restroom smells (loathsomely).

glosses: Followed by like or of if descriptive: to have a particular smell, whether good or bad.
To have a particular tincture or smack of any quality; to savour.

examples.text: A report smells of calumny.
Praises in an enemy are superfluous, or smell of craft.

glosses: To give heed to.

examples.text: So from that tyme forwarde I began to ſmell the word of god, and forſoke the ſchole doctors and ſuch foolries.

glosses: To make a short, audible inhalation, through the nose, as when smelling something.

examples.text: The dog sniffed around the park, searching for a nice scent.
I sniffed the meat to see whether it had gone off.

glosses: To say (something) while sniffing, such as in case of illness or unhappiness, or in contempt.

examples.text: "He's never coming back, is he?" she sniffed while looking at a picture of him.

glosses: To perceive vaguely.

examples.text: I don't know, of course, what your precious Radicals are planning to do, and I don't want to know; but I can sniff trouble in the air, nevertheless.

glosses: To pry; to investigate in an interfering manner.

examples.text: COOMBE: He got the clinch only last week — eighteen months. You see it's no good having anybody here as ain't got a^([sic]) unblemished character. We don't want to have the bluebottles come sniffing round here, do we?

glosses: To be dismissive or contemptuous of something; used with at.

examples.text: This opportunity is not to be sniffed at.

glosses: To intercept and analyse packets of data being transmitted over a network.

examples.text: packet sniffer

glosses: To inhale drugs (usually cocaine) through the nose, usually in powder form.

examples.text: Looks like I picked the wrong week to quit sniffing glue.

glosses: An instance of sniffing.

examples.text: She gave the flowers a quick sniff to check they were real.

glosses: A quantity of something that is inhaled through the nose.
A brief perception, or tiny amount.

examples.text: Tottenham did have a sniff of goal when Defoe's drilled cross just eluded his strike partner at the far post but their best effort came early in the second half when Ryan Fredericks cut in from the right before firing into the side netting.
Telecoms firms want a sniff, having invested heavily in ultra-fast, low-latency 5G spectrum.

glosses: Cocaine.

examples.text: He sold us some sniff and blow.

A short inhalation sound, sometimes associated with crying.
